chunks: Al-Mufaddal narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said:

A dispute occurred between Salmān al-Fārisī, may Allah have mercy on him, and a man. The man said to Salmān: “Who are you, and what are you?” Salmān replied: “As for my beginning and yours, it is a filthy drop; and as for my end and yours, it is a stinking corpse. Then, when the Day of Judgment comes and the scales are set up, whoever’s scales are heavy, he is the noble one; and whoever’s scales are light, he is the vile one.”

key_terms.الْمَوَازِينُ: The scales in which deeds are weighed on the Day of Judgment.
key_terms.ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ: His scales are heavy, meaning his righteous deeds outweigh his evil deeds.
key_terms.جِيفَةٌ مُنْتِنَةٌ: A stinking corpse, describing the body's end after death.
key_terms.خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ: His scales are light, meaning he lacks sufficient righteous deeds.
key_terms.نُطْفَةٌ قَذِرَةٌ: A filthy drop of fluid, describing the humble origin of human creation.
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ: The Day of Judgment, when all people will be raised and judged.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about humility and true honor on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This narration teaches humility by reminding people of their lowly physical origin and their mortal end. True nobility is not based on worldly status, but on one’s deeds when the scales are established on the Day of Judgment.
